summary: Return an activation-stage promotion to fencing when its bound fence proof expires. API impact: existing contract.

guide.reason: The guide already requires a fresh fence proof; this corrects Core retry behavior to enforce that rule.

api.reason: Existing promotion status and retry behavior now return to fencing for expired bound evidence; no route or wire field changed.

roadmap.reason: The source fix does not complete the remaining native S6 or Phase 4 gates.

state.reason: Core owns the durable promotion transfer and fence proofs.
state.record: The existing pool-peer transfer record and operation-bound fence proofs remain authoritative and are reported to a replacement Controller through inventory.

verification.method: TestPoolPromotionRefencesExpiredProofBeforeActivation failed first with no fresh fence call and now passes. Three focused tests cover selective re-fencing and fail-closed malformed and higher-authority cases. Focused tests, go test ./internal/agent (10.606s), and go test -race ./internal/agent (23.845s) passed; independent review cleared the fix. A fresh whole-tree go test -race -count=1 -timeout 20m ./... passed after the correction, as did npm run typecheck, npm test, and the full 374-test Python suite. Native expiry validation held an aged operation-bound proof at activation while the old master was externally off, then replaced it for the same operation, host, target and configuration before promotion completed. A separate retained restart had a new candidate boot identity after proof persistence while retaining the same operation-bound fresh proof byte-identically; the old master stayed off, promotion completed, and cleanup returned it unrestricted. Earlier incomplete fresh-proof attempts are superseded historical evidence.
